summary.intent: Autonomously plan, execute, and ship Phase 63 (Read-Chain Navigation and Rotation Core) of CipherBox while the user was AFK, running the full GSD pipeline: plan-phase → execute-phase → ship-phase.
summary.outcome: Phase 63 fully planned (7 plans, 4 waves, plan-checker PASSED iteration 2), executed (all 7 plans committed, sdk-core 261 passed, sdk 169 passed, live e2e round-trip passed), verified (5/5 must-haves), secured (27/27 threats closed), and PR #579 opened. Ship pipeline was 9/10 complete — CodeRabbit PR review thread resolution was in-flight at transcript end.

repo: The repo squash-merges — PR title is the only commit subject that reaches release-please; individual branch commit subjects with parens in the description don't affect type parsing, so filter-branch reword is unnecessary.
sdk-core has no `typecheck` script; `build` runs `tsup && tsc -p tsconfig.build.json` and is the real type gate. Plans referencing `typecheck` must be redirected.
Port 3000 with `/health` endpoint; CI and plans poll it with `curl -fsS http://localhost:3000/health` — use a bounded health-poll loop, not `sleep 12`.
`gh pr edit` fails on this repo (Projects-classic GraphQL mutation incompatibility) — patch the PR body via `env -u GITHUB_TOKEN gh api -X PATCH repos/FSM1/cipher-box/pulls/<N> -F body=@file`.
GitHub release bot pushes a `chore(release)` commit to the feature branch immediately after `gh pr create` — must `git fetch` + rebase before any further push or it's rejected.
The GSD commit helper reports `commit_failed` as a false-negative; commits actually land. Always verify with `git log --oneline -1`, never blindly retry.
husky pre-commit hooks are slow and regularly exceed the default 2-minute bash timeout — use explicit longer timeouts for git commit commands.

All 6 callers of `updateFolderMetadataAndPublish` omit `nodeId`/`nodeGeneration`, causing every folder metadata update to mint a fresh UUID and reset generation to 0 — breaks node identity continuity.
CodeRabbit bundles findings in both the COMMENTED review body AND as separate inline review threads — must fetch both via REST and GraphQL to get the full set.

89 sdk-e2e tests are intentionally quarantined since Phase 62 under `D-01: SDK runtime stubbed mid-milestone`; re-enable spanning phases 63-65. The Phase-63 deliverable was a single focused test, not lifting the quarantine.

code.finding: Placeholder `new Uint8Array(32)` (all-zeros) passed as `writeKey` to `sealNode`. Safe in Phase 63 because `unsealNode` without a writeKey produces a node with no `writeBody` which `sealNode` skips at `seal.ts:118`. Latent risk: if Phase 65+ calls this path on a node with a writeBody before wiring the real key, the write body reseals under all-zeros.

Uses `childRef.generation` (parent-mirror value), never `childPublished.generation`. Critical generation-source rule per D-06 — the generation must come from the parent's sealed child ref, not the child's published envelope.
`plainKey.fill(0)` present in both success (L43) and catch (L48) paths — intermediate key always zeroed. grant.ts L157 comment incorrectly said 'finally block'; actual implementation uses try/catch.

Anti-malicious-relay guard: both the relay grant set AND `localGrantRecord` are checked independently before triggering rotation. SC#4 zero-rotation invariant: returns 'no-rotation' without calling `deps.rotate` when no covering grant found.
`NodeContent.fileIv` is typed as `string` (hex), validated by codec. CodeRabbit suggestion to change to `Uint8Array` was a false positive — would violate the type contract and break decode.

Had 4 stale `describe.skip('...TODO(phase 63)')` blocks testing the retired `FolderChild`/`encryptFolderMetadata` API under `@ts-nocheck`. All superseded by new active Phase-63 describe blocks with `SealedChildRef` API. Safely deleted in cleanup commit.

workflow: Sequential execution in the main tree (no worktrees) is safer for phases with tight cross-plan coupling and shared test files — avoids node_modules/api:generate leaks documented in project memory.
Running the sdk-core build as an early integration gate between waves is cheap and catches type errors before they compound. Run after Wave 1 and before Wave 3 as checkpoints.

Live e2e suites catch bugs that unit/mock suites miss — 63-07 caught a real engine.ts BFS bug where child `rotateOne` calls received the root's new readKey instead of each child's own derived readKey.

Weekly usage limits can hit mid-execution during long autonomous runs. If it hits near the stated reset time (7am Berlin), retry the failed plan immediately — the tree is left clean on limit-hit (subagent never starts editing).
When the GSD commit helper reports `commit_failed`, verify with `git log --oneline -1` before taking any action. Re-attempting the commit would create a duplicate.

The `pr-release-preview` CI gate parses commit types (feat/fix/test/etc.) from individual commits, not just the PR title. As long as types are valid conventional prefixes, parens in the description text don't trigger rejection.
CodeRabbit re-reviews fix commits pushed after PR creation — triage the second-wave findings with the same operating rule; expect it to surface new issues not in the CLI review.

friction: Weekly usage limit hit mid-execution during plan 63-06, interrupting the phase. The limit reset ~1 minute later (7am Berlin), but required detecting the interruption, assessing tree state, and retrying.
sdk-core `typecheck` script referenced in multiple plans doesn't exist — all three plans (63-05, 63-06) had to be redirected to `build` at runtime.

husky pre-commit hooks regularly exceed 2-minute bash timeout, causing git commit calls to appear to fail (they actually succeed). Required adding explicit longer timeouts and always verifying with `git log`.
`git push` and `git fetch` are blocked in the sandbox; required sandbox-disabled execution for every push operation.
`gh pr edit` is broken for this repo due to Projects-classic GraphQL incompatibility — required workaround via `gh api -X PATCH` with a body file for every PR body update.
CodeRabbit PR review GraphQL `reviewThreads` query returned 0 results when filtering by author, requiring debugging and a fallback approach to fetch threads.
GitHub release bot pushes `chore(release)` immediately after `gh pr create` — any push without fetching first is rejected; requires a `git fetch` + rebase step that wasn't originally in the plan.
